objective: Automatically retain bounded local diagnostics for ordinary play and provide an observable, isolated, mouse-driven playtest loop usable by inexpensive coding agents.

requirements.description: Ordinary world launches record session/build/content/save identity, real commands and failures, travel/combat/rewards/progression, sampled performance and generation timings, periodic snapshots, markers and managed crash context without changing RNG, save compatibility or gameplay.
Recording is local, bounded, fail-open and optional; retention protects live sessions, diagnostics never open or overwrite player saves, and interrupted recordings remain inspectable.

A versioned observe/action protocol drives the actual mouse input pipeline, exposes only player-visible information, reports stale/invalid actions, and retains screenshots/actions/results with isolated saves.

A reproducible automated playtest suite exercises exploration, contextual actions, markers, combat and failure feedback; a bounded optional Codex loop accepts an explicit model/reasoning setting and produces evidence-linked findings.

Shared developer commands discover and report sessions, feedback and agent artifacts; documentation explains use, source/version identity, platform limits and the difference between automated assertions and model opinions.
